rules.enforces: every check script has a registry entry (or a reasoned unregistered_ok line), its paths and owner doc exist, ids are unique, and docs/rules.md matches the registry
rules.why: checks piled up with no record of which rule each protects or why it exists, so rules in docs drifted from what actually fails

rules.enforces: every analytics event name a call site emits exists in Resources/analytics-events.psv
rules.why: AnalyticsReporter drops events missing from the PSV registry with no local sign; meeting_capture_stopped_under_controller read zero fleet-wide that way (e49fd4298, PR #1699)

rules.enforces: the daily audio-reliability script, the issue-500 manual proof doc, the QA bench packet and the smoke source lists name the same lanes and files
rules.why: this was a Swift test reading scripts and docs as text, so only a Mac found drift; moved to a repo check (2d2c102e1, PR #2049)

rules.enforces: every file named in the hand-kept swiftc source lists (fast tests, smokes) exists
rules.why: hand-kept lists rotted when files moved and the break showed up only in a Mac compile; one of ten red Swift CI runs in the week before PR #1884 was a list missing a new file (6cc8f8766, PR #1181)

rules.enforces: the debug test control channel stays behind TRANSCRIPTED_DEBUG_CONTROL, which only build.sh sets; build-beta.sh refuses the flag and greps the binary
rules.why: the agent control surface can start recordings and change settings, so shipping it would be a remote-control hole in user builds (5268a6874, PR #2208)

rules.enforces: every backticked repo path in a tracked Markdown file exists, and the always-loaded entry docs stay within their line budget
rules.why: agents follow doc paths; entry docs had grown to 641 lines across three overlapping guides with dead pointers (1b432fc79, PR #1885)

rules.enforces: no Swift file declares the same symbol twice in one scope
rules.why: git auto-merges produced duplicate declarations (a doubled `let remindSize` in CapturePillController) that syntax-only parsing misses, so they failed 15-25 minutes into the Mac build (8103de399, PR #1490)

rules.enforces: no new Swift file over 800 lines; files in .agents/file-size-baseline.json only shrink
rules.why: big files are where agents lose the thread and merges collide; hotspot files had passed 1,500 lines (7de37226d, PR #1951)

rules.enforces: every Tools/* Swift package runs in a GitHub workflow and has a rule in .agents/test-matrix.yml (or a reviewed reason in TOOLS_WITHOUT_CI)
rules.why: AGENTS.md said a new Tools package needs CI, and nothing failed when someone forgot (9610d0330, PR #1884)

rules.enforces: every root *.sh command is listed in docs/repo-layout.md
rules.why: agents find commands from the layout doc; an unlisted wrapper is invisible to them (9610d0330, PR #1884)

rules.enforces: agent guides live in AGENTS.md only: a tracked CLAUDE.md may only be the bare `@AGENTS.md` stub, and no CLAUDE.local.md exists
rules.why: a CLAUDE.md is read instead of AGENTS.md, so a second copy of the rules drifted from the first (9615ec201, PR #1947)

rules.enforces: a Tools package pulling FluidAudio from SwiftPM pins the same version as FLUID_AUDIO_VERSION in build-deps.sh
rules.why: a bundled helper could run an older FluidAudio than the app, with nothing to flag it (648273bfa, PR #1954)

rules.enforces: a Sources/ or Tests/ Swift comment that names a repo .md path points at a file that exists
rules.why: renamed docs left dead "read X first" pointers in code comments (648273bfa, PR #1954)

rules.enforces: a Sources/ file names only types from modules its module may depend on in .agents/modules.json; every Sources/ file belongs to a module; no baseline, any crossing fails
rules.why: the app is one Swift target, so the compiler let any file use any type and 70 crossings piled up (7de37226d, PR #1951); the last were removed and the baseline dropped in PR #2173

rules.enforces: the QA CLI's permission-state command, its probe matrix, the bench script and docs agree that blocked automation reports INCOMPLETE, never green
rules.why: a QA run blocked by macOS TCC could look green; the old guard was a Swift source-text test (b27ae5dd4, PR #2092 via #2173)

rules.enforces: a change doesn't break a Swift test that reads a repo file as text and pins a literal; the number of such pins in .agents/source-pin-baseline.json only shrinks
rules.why: editing a pinned file turned Mac-only CI red with no way to see it on Linux (b2d7d0320, PR #1805)

rules.enforces: before a repair or reland branch is opened, the original change isn't already merged under this or another PR (exit 3 means it landed)
rules.why: six PRs were wasted when two threads re-opened repair branches for #1457 and #1471 after those changes had already merged (16ecf7c93, PR #1485)

rules.enforces: the three CaptureLibraryPathSafety.swift copies stay byte-identical
rules.why: if one copy drifts, build units disagree about which capture-library paths are safe; the old guard was a Swift source-text test (0be69e1b0, PR #2091)

rules.enforces: no allowlisted telemetry key contains a fragment the off-device sanitizers drop (audio, error, file, name, path, text, title, token, url, ...)
rules.why: start_profile was allowlisted but never arrived because "profile" contains "file" (196e7456d, PR #1805)

rules.enforces: no new test that reads Sources/ as text or asserts on wall-clock time; counts in .agents/test-shape-baseline.json only shrink
rules.why: in the week before PR #1884, 2 of 10 red Swift CI runs were a wall-clock test on a busy runner, and about 1 in 5 fast-test files read app code as text (9610d0330, PR #1884)

rules.enforces: every Tests/quarantine.txt line is `date | existing suite | reason`; entries older than two weeks warn
rules.why: flaky suites got retried until green instead of fixed or benched; the bench list needs real suite names to mean anything (9610d0330, PR #1884)

rules.enforces: every transcripted.<area>.<name> accessibility identifier the QA smokes and build.sh's launch smoke press is declared in the app
rules.why: a removed identifier failed the smoke only on a Mac with the app running, long after the change; the old guard was a source-text test (8b2e6286b, PR #2073 via #2173)

rules.enforces: every NSWindow/NSPanel surface in Sources/ is listed in .agents/window-inventory.json with a screen-sharing policy, and sets sharingType to match
rules.why: AppKit windows are readable by screen sharing by default, so a new transcript panel could leak live text into a shared screen (ab664240f, PR #2244, issue #2132)

rules.enforces: Swift 6 strict-concurrency warnings per Sources/ folder stay at or under .agents/concurrency-baseline.json
rules.enforcer: bash scripts/dev/concurrency-census.sh && python3 scripts/dev/concurrency-census.py --log build/concurrency-census.log --mode check
rules.why: the app still builds in Swift 5 mode, so data races and wrong-thread calls only warn under a strict typecheck; without a count they grew unseen (9610d0330, PR #1884)

rules.enforces: synthetic secrets planted in logs, events, Sentry/PostHog payloads, QA reports, PR/release text and handoff summaries don't come out the other side
rules.why: local-first is the product promise; this sweeps every report and handoff surface for raw user content before it leaves (e0376ebba, PR #1004)

rules.enforces: repo, release and update drift, cask/appcast parity, PostHog schema drift, raw observability keys, entitlements, shell hazards and recent-history secrets all pass; strict release-health fixture matches Info.plist
rules.why: the nightly security checker had gone missing and was restored with a shared sanitizer corpus (68e84492c, PR #584); 6 of 10 red Swift CI runs before PR #1884 were it tripping on half-finished release PRs, so linux-checks now runs it only when release surfaces change

rules.enforces: app and Resources size, bundled-model presence, launch-to-interactive, dictation start/stop and meeting throughput stay within budget
rules.why: a performance audit found heavy launch work and a bundled model bloating normal builds; the budgets keep those wins from sliding back (980d36068, PR #707)

rules.enforces: tests for Swift policy files actually catch small breaks (mutants are KILLED, not SURVIVED)
rules.why: tests that pass with the code broken looked like coverage; the probe finds missing assertions (924cf9dd8, PR #1884)

rules.enforces: a PR merged by the auto-merge gate may change a debt baseline (.agents/*-baseline.json) only to lower counts or drop entries, never the concurrency baseline
rules.why: without it a cleanup-lane PR could raise its own baseline and merge with no owner review (e6005dafb, PR #2039)

rules.enforces: app-launch smokes run only in a separate OS account, a verified hosted runner, or the throwaway Mac runner VM, so they can't read or write the owner's preferences
rules.why: native QA launches could run as the active macOS account and use its real preferences (8d4685290, PR #1757); HOME and CFFIXED_USER_HOME overrides don't stop UserDefaults resolving through that account's cfprefsd session, extended to the launch benchmark for issue #2256

rules.enforces: build.sh and build-beta.sh refuse to delete build/Transcripted.app while that bundle is running (FORCE_REBUILD_RUNNING=1 overrides)
rules.why: the owner often runs the app straight from a worktree's build/, and a rebuild deleted the running bundle out from under it (648273bfa, PR #1954)

rules.enforces: Sentry and PostHog events carry only allowlisted keys and tags; everything else is dropped before it leaves the device
rules.why: Sentry and PostHog are bounded integrations; raw transcript text, titles, names and paths must never reach them, so the only way out is through one sanitizer each

rules.enforces: an outgoing push adds no term from the private denylist outside the repo (~/.config/transcripted/public-repo-denylist.txt) in diffs, commit messages or branch names
rules.why: private research names and people's details must never land in a public repo, and history can't be quietly cleaned once pushed

rules.enforces: no I/O, locks, allocations or ObjC calls inside CoreAudio real-time callbacks; deep-copy buffers before any async hop
rules.why: a blocked or allocating render callback drops audio; nothing mechanical sees what runs on the IO thread yet

rules.enforces: code that builds an AVAudioEngine or touches inputNode says what happens when a Bluetooth headset is the default input
rules.why: a fresh engine's inputNode binds the default input; with AirPods that flips them into call mode and garbles audio, the cause of every AirPods garble bug so far (audio-tap-install-unguarded covers only tap installs)

rules.enforces: session controllers and UI state are @MainActor; capture internals use DispatchQueue + NSLock
rules.why: wrong-thread UI and session access races; main-actor-blocking-io and concurrency-census cover parts, not the rule itself

rules.enforces: simplification doesn't delete, hide or bury meeting detection, the Speakers directory, per-app Auto Enter, model-cache cleanup, status-item right-click or retained-audio playback without owner approval
rules.why: cleanup passes have removed features users relied on; this is a judgment call no check can make

rules.enforces: scripts, labs and tests never write to the real capture library or prefs; anything that deletes checks the path is under the root it owns
rules.why: a harness touching real state can destroy saved meetings; native-smoke-account-isolation covers app-launch smokes and the harness-delete-outside-owned-root lint covers deletes in harness code, but writes to real state are still judgment

rules.enforces: agent commits for the owner use the owner's noreply identity as author and committer, with no AI Co-authored-by trailers
rules.why: commit credit is the owner's call; nothing checks author identity

rules.enforces: owner work rebases onto origin/main, runs check.sh, then pushes HEAD:main; never force-push; a red main is fixed forward or reverted by the session that broke it
rules.why: PRs for owner work were slow; direct pushes trade that for a red-main risk the session must own

rules.enforces: meaningful code gets an independent diff review (codex review or /code-review) before the push, with the verdict in the commit message
rules.why: landing straight on main skips PR review, so this is the only second look

rules.enforces: a cleanup/ or garden/ change is behavior-neutral: no logic, access-level, init-order or isolation changes during a move
rules.why: cleanup lanes auto-merge, so a hidden behavior change would ship without the owner seeing it

rules.enforces: docs/appcast.xml and Casks/transcripted.rb change only in a release the owner asked for, cut from a commit with green Swift CI
rules.why: Sparkle reads the appcast straight from main, so any push to it ships to every install at once

rules.enforces: a flaky test is fixed or benched in Tests/quarantine.txt the same day; never retry until green
rules.why: retry-until-green hides real failures; test-quarantine-format checks the bench list, not the habit
